records.text: An Associated Press report said the 2008 Kirkwood City Hall shooting killed two police officers and three city officials, critically injured the mayor, wounded a reporter, and ended when police killed Charles Thornton.
records.speaker: The Associated Press

appearances.snippet: Sirens wail outside Kirkwood City Hall in Missouri. The building that usually houses mundane civic meetings became the scene of a rampage Thursday night after a gunman stormed the building and opened fire. ... Two police officers and three city officials were killed, the mayor was critically hurt and a newspaper reporter was wounded. ... The shooter was eventually shot and killed by police. By police. It's reported he was Charles Cookie Thornton, who had a reputation for disrupting city meetings and for making outrageous statements.

verification.notes: Contemporaneous AP reporting states that Charles Thornton killed two police officers and three city officials, critically wounded Mayor Mike Swoboda, wounded a reporter, and was shot and killed by police.

sources.title: Associated Press via ABC News: Gunman With a Gripe Exacts Revenge at City Hall
sources.relevance: Contemporaneous AP account matching the quoted casualty and police-response details.

records.text: Charles Thornton believed the Kirkwood police were racist and were running a plantation.
records.speaker: Justin Streiff

appearances.snippet: He thought the police were racist in the town. ... You always heard him saying that he thought the police were running a plantation.

records.text: Everyone in Kirkwood knew Charles Thornton was kind of crazy, but no one thought it would reach the point of a shooting.
records.speaker: Justin Streiff

appearances.snippet: Everyone knows he's kind of kind of crazy and I mean, I don't think anyone ever thought it would get to this point.
